full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs, in brief, is that, one Fazle Ali Mridha was the owner of the land stated in the 1st and 2nd schedules to the plaint and the CS khatian No. 673 was accordingly, prepared in his name; that thereafter he mortgaged first schedule land to Wahidullah, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in consideration of Taka 200 and that required "Tamshuk Patra Dalil" was registered on 13-6-1929 copulating interest to be paid Taka 1.50% per month and also stipulated that Fazle Ali Mridha would not transfer to other person unless the consideration money would be paid along with interest. It is further contended that Fazle Ali could not realise the aforesaid money and moreover, he created a "Belawaznama" deed in favour of his two wives namely, Atarernessa Bibi and Nekjan Bibi and also created a 'Safkabala' deed in favour of his foster daughter Hasmaternessa Bibi and son-in-law Nadir Ali in respect of the suit land for the purpose of saving the suit land from further auction sale due to his deftness; that in this circumstances Wahidullah filed a Arbitration Case No. 83 of 1938 against Fazle Ali Mridha to realize the cot money; that Fazle Ali Mridha admitted about the debt but later on he died before realization of debt; that the heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha i.e. his two wives, foster daughter and son-in-law sold the property to Wahidullah vide registered kabala deed dated 4-4-1940 in consideration of Taka 300 amongst which Taka 200 was setoff with the debt and received rest of Taka 100 and handed over the possession of the land to Wahidullah and that the aforesaid heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha sold the 2nd schedule land to Wahidullah vide registered deed dated 18-6-1941. It is also added that having the ownership of the land, Wahidullah died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and plaintiff Nos. 8 to 10 and others and accordingly, SA record was prepared in the names of his sons and daughters; that thereafter the Tasdik record was also prepared in the names of plaintiffs; that in the meantime the plaintiff No. 1 constructed semi-pucca building in the plot No. 2065 in the year of 1991 and 1992 and started to live there appointing one Babul Miah as caretaker and that a holding No. 38 /Ka was opened in Laksham Pourashava in the name of plaintiff No. 1 as the house was created in schedule No. 2ka and 2Kha . The further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant Nos. 1, 5, 6, 7 and 10 to 12 hired persons and threatened to dispossess the caretaker Babul Mia and that then Babul Mia lodged a GD entry with Laksham Police Station and that police held enquiry and filed an application before the Magistrate Court for appointing a receiver. The Magistrate appointed the Officer-in-Charge of Laksham Police Station as receiver. The receiver on 27-5-1997 attached the suit property in preparing seizure list. Thereafter, the defendants filed Criminal Revision case before the learned District Judge for setting aside the appointment of receiver with direction to hand over the possession to the defendants, then the aforesaid caretaker ran up to the Appellate Division but all went in vain. 

 7. The plaintiffs filed CS khatian (Exhibit 1), deed dated 31-3-1940 executed by Atarernessa in favour of Md. Wahidullah (Exhibit 2), deed dated 18-6-1941 executed by Atarernessa in favour of Wahidullah (Exhibit 3), deed dated 9-6-1949 executed by Badsha Miah in favour of Wahidullah (Exhibit 4), SA khatian (Exhibit 5), Dakhilas (Exhibit 6, 6(ka) to 6(Na), tax receipts of Pourashava (Exhibit 7), certificate given by Chairman, Pourshava (Exhibit 7(Ka) and certified copy of the judgment and decree in title Suit No. 356 of 1994 of Subordinate Judge Court (Exhibits 8 and 8(Ka)) in support of their contention. 

 19. It is admitted that the suit land appertaining to CS khatian No. 673 originally belonged to Fazle Ali Mridha who mortgaged the same to Wahiduddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and that a Tamshuk patra deed was registered on 13-6-1929 to that end. It is also admitted that Fazle Ali Mridha without repaying mortgage money transferred some portion of the suit land in favour of his two wives namely, Atorernesga and Nekjan Bibi and by a habanera deed also transferred the other portion in favour of his foster daughter and son-in-law and that in the circumstances, Wahidulah filed an Arbitration case against Fazle Ali Mridha to realise the cot money. 

 22. The plaintiffs have filed CS khatian Exhibit 1, deed dated 31-3-1940 executed by Atorernessa in favour of Md Wahidullah, Exhibit 2, deed dated 18-6-1941 executed by Atorernessa in favour of Wahidullah. 

 35. On the other hand, PW 1 Ekramullah Chowdhury, son of Wahidullah Chowdhury, deposed that his father purchased the suit by virtue of kabala dated 4-4-1940 and kabala dated 18-6-1941 and got possession of the suit land; that after getting possession, he sold one decimal from plot No. 2077 and 48 decimals from plot No. 2078 to Tarab Ali and others who have been possessing the land since purchase, that his father also sold 49.5 decimals to Badsha Miah by virtue of Kabala dated 1-6-1949 and thus Badsha Miah has been possessing some portion of the suit land peacefully. He further deposed that he had been possessing the rest of the suit land creating semi-pucca building and tin-shed house thereon till taking over the possessing by the Receiver on 28-1-2001; that SA khatian being No. 691 Exhibit 5 was prepared in their names; that they paid rent and rent receipts were marked Exhibit 6 series; that during Bangladesh survey their names were recorded; that his brother also sold 23½ decimals of land to Torab Ali who has been also possessing the same; that Municipal holding was prepared in their names and they paid taxes and their tax receipts are marked Exhibit 7 series. He further testified that when defendants No. 1, 5 to 7 and others attempted to dispossess the caretaker of the plaintiffs on 17-5-1997, then the caretaker filed a GD entry in Laksham PS on 21-5-1997; that on the basis of the report of OC Laksham, Magistrate appointed OC, Laksham as Receiver who took possession from his care-taker; but being biased Officer-in-Charge, Laksham reported that he took possession of the defendants' land; that subsequently, appointment of Receiver was cancelled who handed over possession of the suit land to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and that the defendants had no possession before taking possession from the Receiver. Nothing could be elicited to shake his credibility in any manner whatsoever. 

 42. The plaintiffs have proved their possession till taking over the possession by the Receiver and such assertion has not only been proved by oral evidence but also by documentary evidence. SA khatian and draft khatian of Bangladesh were prepared in the names of the plaintiffs. Mutation, opening of municipal holding, rent receipts and municipal taxes are also the documentary evidence of possession.
